name: BAGGS & MARSHALL RES - HOUSE

nadir.desc: The nadir view shows a large residential property set well back from a two-lane paved road that curves along the upper-left portion of the image, with a long curved driveway connecting the road to the structure cluster near the center of the parcel|The main residence and at least one detached structure are visible, along with a small patch of green lawn to the south of the main building and a tan-colored paved or compacted surface area adjacent to the structures|The surrounding terrain is open high-desert scrubland with scattered low shrubs and juniper trees throughout the parcel and on neighboring properties|No fencing, gates, or pools are visible from this view, and the parcel is large with significant open ground on all sides of the structures.

alpha.desc: The alpha view highlights the front of the property, showing the curved driveway as it approaches from the paved road at the lower portion of the view and leads to the main residence and a detached structure to the left|The main residence has a light-colored exterior with a dark roof, and multiple rooflines indicate a multi-wing or irregular-footprint structure|Scattered juniper trees are distributed across the front approach, and the driveway surface is tan-colored and compacted, wide enough for a single vehicle|The street frontage along the paved road is open with no visible gate or barrier controlling driveway access.

bravo.desc: The bravo view shows the right side of the property from the east, with the residence visible in the right-center portion of the frame and the road running along the far right edge|A cleared sandy area is visible to the rear-left of the structures, and scattered juniper trees are distributed across the open terrain on this side of the parcel|No fencing, outbuildings, or secondary access routes are visible on the right side of the property|The ground surface on this side is open desert with no visible obstructions between the road and the structure.

charlie.desc: The charlie view shows the rear of the property, with the main residence visible near the upper center of the frame and the road running along the top edge of the image|The rear of the structure shows multiple rooflines and what appears to be a detached or attached accessory structure to the right of the main building|A small patch of lawn is visible to the front-left of the structures in this perspective, and scattered juniper trees surround the building cluster on the rear side|No fencing or barriers are visible along the rear of the property, and the terrain between the rear of the structures and the road is open scrubland.

delta.desc: The delta view shows the left side of the property with the road running along the far left edge and the residence and detached structure visible in the left-center of the frame|A tan compacted surface area is clearly visible adjacent to the structures, consistent with a parking or staging area|Juniper trees are scattered throughout the left side of the parcel but do not form a continuous barrier between the road and the structures|No fencing, gates, or secondary access points are visible on this side of the property.

considerations: The property is accessed via a single curved driveway connecting directly to a paved two-lane road, with no visible gate or barrier at the driveway entrance, allowing unobstructed vehicle access. The driveway and adjacent compacted surface area near the structures provide space for apparatus staging. The surrounding terrain is open desert scrubland with scattered juniper trees, which do not obstruct approach routes but present surface considerations for off-road movement. The residence sits well back from the road, requiring responders to travel the full length of the curved driveway to reach the structure.
clarifications: Is the driveway surface compacted gravel or paved, and can it support the weight of a fully loaded fire apparatus or ambulance? Are there any gates, keypad entries, or access controls at the driveway entrance not visible in current imagery? Does the detached structure have its own entry points, and is it accessible independently of the main residence? Is the compacted tan surface area adjacent to the structures usable as a turnaround for large vehicles? Are there any low-clearance features such as overhead utilities or tree limbs along the driveway that would restrict tall apparatus?
